projects.Use Case: In-orbit AI and remote-sensing processing
projects.Project Summary: First constellation launched for a planned 1,000-satellite space-computing network intended to process AI and remote-sensing workloads in orbit.
projects.Scale: First constellation launched; 1,000 satellites targeted
projects.Economic Mechanism: Capacity expansion
projects.Notes: Legacy v1 record; target scale is prospective and commercial operating date was not disclosed.

projects.Use Case: AI-ready data hall design
projects.Project Summary: Beacon Point data-hall redesign around Nvidia architecture increased planned capacity within the same land and utility footprint.
projects.Scale: Phase 2 first hall expected Q2 2028
projects.Economic Mechanism: Capacity expansion
projects.Notes: Legacy v1 record; metric is company-reported and the broader lease is not treated as realized revenue.

projects.Use Case: HBM advanced packaging and testing for AI accelerators
projects.Project Summary: SK hynix broke ground on its West Lafayette, Indiana advanced HBM packaging facility, its first U.S. HBM production base, integrating Korean wafer production with U.S. packaging, testing and an advanced-packaging R&D testbed.
projects.Scale: Over $4B investment; cleanroom targeted Oct. 2028; next-generation HBM mass production targeted H2 2029
projects.Economic Mechanism: Capacity expansion and U.S. AI-memory supply-chain localization
projects.Notes: Groundbreaking occurred Aug. 27 local time. Primary source published Aug. 28 Seoul time. Do not treat planned production or job creation as realized outcomes.

projects.Use Case: Robotic data-center maintenance and operations
projects.Project Summary: Meta is piloting robots inside live data centers to automate technician tasks including network-cable handling, server power cycling, component reseating, rack movement and equipment inspection.
projects.Scale: Trials span Altoona, Iowa and Prometheus in New Albany, Ohio; two Watney dual-arm units have handled supervised cabling work in Altoona since June 2025, with ABB and Kinova systems tested for other maintenance tasks.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce manual maintenance workload and improve incident response as AI data-center footprint scales
projects.Notes: Wired reports the specific trials from current and former workers; Meta declined to comment on the individual tests. Do not treat worker estimates of potential labor displacement as company targets or measured outcomes.

projects.Use Case: AI-agent control of scientific and engineering hardware
projects.Project Summary: Anthropic opened a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard, developed from work with HHMI Janelia, to let AI agents discover and operate programmable laboratory and advanced-manufacturing equipment through a shared interface; partner tests include microscopy, drug-discovery assays and quantum-hardware calibration.
projects.Scale: Research preview with scientific and advanced-manufacturing partners; early tests include HHMI Janelia, Genentech, Carnegie Mellon and QuEra.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce bespoke hardware-integration work and enable more autonomous experimental workflows
projects.Enabling Vendors: HHMI Janelia; Genentech; Carnegie Mellon University; QuEra
projects.Notes: Treat partner-reported preview results as early pilot evidence, not proof of general autonomous-lab reliability. MHS remains a limited research preview and is not yet open source.

projects.Use Case: Dedicated AI compute capacity for Anthropic at Monarch Compute Campus
projects.Project Summary: Nscale is developing the Monarch Compute Campus in Mason County, West Virginia, and high-quality reporting says Anthropic has contracted roughly 460 MW of Nvidia Vera Rubin compute there under a six-year agreement expected to begin serving in late 2027.
projects.Scale: 2,250-acre campus with an onsite microgrid scalable to over 8 GW; Anthropic reportedly contracted ~460 MW for six years
projects.Economic Mechanism: Secure dedicated powered AI compute capacity while reducing dependence on conventional grid interconnection
projects.Notes: Nscale's primary materials confirm the Monarch site and onsite-power design; the Anthropic tenant terms are from Reuters/FT reporting rather than a company announcement. Do not treat the 460 MW as online until later operating evidence confirms delivery.

projects.Use Case: Autonomous passenger mobility for travelers with reduced mobility
projects.Project Summary: After a 10-unit trial from March 2025 through 2026, Changi moved WHILL Autonomous Service into full deployment, with airport operations staff dispatching autonomous wheelchairs to transport reduced-mobility passengers between gates and the Special Service Lounge.
projects.Scale: Up to 18 autonomous wheelchairs progressively deployed across Terminal 2 and 3 transit areas; prior trial fleet of 10 units
projects.Economic Mechanism: Expand passenger-assistance capacity while reducing continuous one-to-one escort requirements
projects.Notes: The 18-unit figure is a progressive first-phase deployment target; WHILL's more than one million autonomous rides is platform-wide and should not be treated as a Changi-specific result.

projects.Use Case: Sovereign GPU-as-a-service for AI training and inference
projects.Project Summary: HUMAIN put AMD Instinct MI355X and EPYC compute with Cisco Silicon One networking into production in Saudi Arabia, with the platform now serving customers for AI training and inference as the partners prepare a larger joint-venture buildout.
projects.Scale: Production MI355X infrastructure live; next phase up to 250 MW beginning in 2027; joint-venture target up to 1 GW by 2030
projects.Economic Mechanism: Expand locally operated sovereign AI compute supply and sell GPU-as-a-service
projects.Notes: Current live capacity was not disclosed. Treat the 250 MW and 1 GW figures as prospective targets, not online capacity.

projects.Use Case: AI-ready data center capacity at Oxagon, NEOM
projects.Project Summary: HUMAIN and DataVolt began construction on 100 MW of an AI-ready data center at Oxagon, NEOM, within a 360 MW first phase designed for high-density AI and cloud workloads.
projects.Scale: 100 MW under development within a 360 MW first phase; wider DataVolt Oxagon campus planned at 1.5 GW
projects.Economic Mechanism: Create high-density AI-ready capacity with access to energy, cooling and subsea connectivity for deployable compute
projects.Notes: Construction is underway, but the first 100 MW is not yet operating. The 360 MW first phase and 1.5 GW wider campus are prospective scale figures.

projects.Use Case: Fully autonomous ride-hailing
projects.Project Summary: Waymo began welcoming public riders to fully autonomous rides in Denver, San Diego and Tampa, expanding its operating service to 14 cities.
projects.Scale: First public riders in Denver, San Diego and Tampa; 14 cities providing fully autonomous trips; tens of thousands signed up in each new city
projects.Economic Mechanism: Expand autonomous ride-hailing service across additional metropolitan markets
projects.Notes: Public access is expanding gradually in the three cities; do not treat each market as fully open to everyone yet.

projects.Use Case: 24/7 geothermal power for potential Google data-center capacity in Utah
projects.Project Summary: Fervo signed a 396 MW power purchase agreement with Google tied to the Cape Station enhanced-geothermal GeoCluster in Utah, which is expected to come online in 2028 and is intended to support a potential Google data center.
projects.Scale: 396 MW contracted; Google has an option for ~600 MW more by June 2030, for nearly 1 GW total; the additional option is not committed capacity
projects.Economic Mechanism: Add firm 24/7 electricity capacity for AI/data-center load and enable potential Utah data-center development
projects.Notes: Google's Utah data-center plans remain conditional on engineering feasibility, state and local approvals, and commercial conditions. Do not treat the optional additional ~600 MW as committed capacity.

projects.Use Case: AI ambient clinical documentation
projects.Project Summary: BJC Health and WashU Medicine expanded Abridge across BJC Health's East Region after a 450-clinician rollout and evaluation, with approximately 4,000 clinicians now able to use the platform for AI-generated clinical documentation.
projects.Scale: Expanded from 450 clinicians in 2025 to ~4,000 clinicians across BJC Health's East Region
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce clinician documentation time and after-hours administrative work
projects.Measured Metric: After-hours documentation time reduction by day 150
projects.Notes: Encounter-level pilot evaluation reported overall documentation time reduction rising from 8% initially to 15% by day 150 and after-hours documentation reduction from 6% to 20%. Treat these as BJC/WashU pilot results, not system-wide or industry-wide effects.

projects.Use Case: Autonomous heavy-cargo delivery under FAA eVTOL pilot program
projects.Project Summary: Elroy Air's Chaparral conducted a week-long series of uncrewed autonomous cargo flights in Houma, Louisiana under the FAA eVTOL Integration Pilot Program, carrying mixed cargo under Air Traffic Control oversight.
projects.Scale: Week-long late-August flight series in Houma; Chaparral rated for >500 lb payload and up to 450-mile range
projects.Economic Mechanism: Enable heavy middle-mile cargo delivery without onboard pilots or conventional airport/runway infrastructure
projects.Notes: FAA described the demonstration as the first remotely piloted aircraft test flight under eIPP; Elroy described the week-long series as autonomous and uncrewed. This is a regulatory integration pilot, not commercial certification or scaled service.

projects.Use Case: Commercial GPU compute from repurposed mining infrastructure
projects.Project Summary: EcoHash completed AI-infrastructure retrofits within Cango's owned Georgia facility, powered on an initial batch of GPU servers and began providing commercial GPU compute services while additional GPU deployment continues.
projects.Scale: Dedicated AI section at owned 50 MW Georgia facility supports up to 3 MW; first batch of GPU servers is operating commercially; additional GPU deployment is ongoing.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Repurpose an already-powered mining site and modular compute containers to shorten AI-capacity deployment time and sell commercial GPU compute.
projects.Notes: The up-to-3 MW figure is infrastructure capacity, not evidence that 3 MW of GPUs are installed or utilized. The initial customer is not named; commercial service has begun using part of the first GPU batch.

projects.Use Case: Supervised autonomous ride-hailing
projects.Project Summary: Uber and Wayve launched supervised autonomous rides in London, allowing normal Uber riders to be matched with Wayve-equipped vehicles operating in live passenger service while a licensed safety driver remains onboard.
projects.Scale: Small initial fleet operating across London except airports; more than 140,000 Londoners had opted in for Wayve ride matching at launch.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Add autonomous-vehicle supply to the ride-hailing network and validate operating readiness before broader driverless scale.
projects.Notes: The launch is supervised: a trained TfL-licensed private-hire driver remains onboard. Public access is real but the initial fleet is deliberately small and not yet driverless; opt-ins are demand interest, not completed rides.

projects.Use Case: Company-wide personal AI agent for cross-application knowledge work
projects.Project Summary: Cisco is rolling out MyAgent across its workforce as a governed personal AI agent that can coordinate supervised autonomous workflows across Outlook, Webex, Jira, SharePoint and other enterprise systems using approved models, agents and company data through the Circuit platform.
projects.Scale: Rolling out to 90,000 employees; cross-application supervised workflows on Cisco's Circuit platform
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce manual coordination and repetitive knowledge-work steps by letting employees delegate objectives across enterprise applications under governed human oversight
projects.Notes: Cisco says MyAgent is rolling out to 90,000 employees, but availability is not the same as active usage. The disclosed nearly 350% quarter-over-quarter growth refers to agentic interactions on Circuit broadly, not a MyAgent-specific productivity result.

projects.Use Case: Reserved GPU inference capacity for production AI and agentic workloads
projects.Project Summary: QumulusAI completed deployment of 616 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Runpod under one- and two-year reserved-capacity agreements, with all 77 GPU nodes active and served from QumulusAI's existing U.S. data-center footprint.
projects.Scale: 616 GPUs across 77 active nodes; full deployment reached in August 2026 ahead of the Sept. 1 target
projects.Economic Mechanism: Expand contracted inference capacity for Runpod customers using distributed existing data-center infrastructure and workload-matched GPU architecture
projects.Notes: All 77 contracted GPU nodes are active and the deployment finished ahead of schedule. This verifies delivery of reserved compute capacity, not customer utilization, revenue realization, or broader demand saturation.

projects.Use Case: High-density AI data-center capacity for frontier AI companies and hyperscalers
projects.Project Summary: HyperVault, a Tata Consultancy Services subsidiary, secured 264 acres in Hyderabad for a phased AI data-center campus designed for high-density GPU training, inference and advanced-computing workloads, with capacity planned up to 1 GW.
projects.Scale: 264-acre Hyderabad campus; up to 1 GW planned capacity; up to INR 700 billion ($7.4B) planned investment; phased build
projects.Economic Mechanism: Expand AI-ready compute capacity for training and inference workloads
projects.Notes: Land is secured, but construction progress and online capacity were not disclosed. Treat the up-to-1-GW capacity and investment figures as prospective, not operating capacity.

projects.Use Case: Purpose-built driverless robotaxi service
projects.Project Summary: Tesla began commercial deployment of a small number of Cybercab vehicles in Austin, Texas, with rides available in limited areas through the Robotaxi service; Cybercab is purpose-built for autonomous operation without conventional manual controls.
projects.Scale: Small initial commercial deployment in limited areas of Austin; expansion is planned gradually
projects.Economic Mechanism: Operate commercial ride-hailing with a purpose-built autonomous vehicle and no onboard human driver
projects.Notes: NHTSA Audit Query AQ26002 remains open. On Sept. 15, NHTSA required Tesla to answer detailed certification and operating questions by Sept. 30, including whether temporary manual controls were used in its compliance basis. This is not a finding of noncompliance or a recall. Do not treat limited Austin availability as scaled service.

projects.Use Case: Secure enterprise generative AI for planning, logistics, policy and administration
projects.Project Summary: The U.S. Department of War expanded GenAI.mil into a multi-model enterprise AI platform by launching ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government alongside Gemini, giving personnel secure AI tools for document-heavy planning, policy, logistics, administration and other daily workflows.
projects.Scale: Department-wide GenAI.mil platform; ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government launched; built to support more than 3 million civilian and military personnel
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce routine knowledge-work time and improve knowledge continuity across planning, logistics and administration
projects.Notes: ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government are accredited at Impact Level 5 for Controlled Unclassified Information. The platform is built to support more than 3 million personnel, but that capacity is not evidence that all personnel are active users, and no measured productivity result was disclosed.

projects.Use Case: AI-assisted cyber defense for state, local and water-system operators
projects.Project Summary: OpenAI and MS-ISAC launched a public-sector and water-focused Daybreak pilot that pairs frontier cyber-model access with guided training and hands-on support to help state, local, tribal, territorial and water-system defenders validate findings, prioritize vulnerabilities and coordinate remediation.
projects.Scale: Initial group of public-sector and water-system defenders; participant count not disclosed
projects.Economic Mechanism: Increase defensive capacity by reducing the time and specialized effort needed to validate vulnerabilities and coordinate fixes
projects.Notes: Pilot participant count and measured outcomes were not disclosed. The broader $1 billion Daybreak commitment and existing Daybreak user counts should not be treated as results or scale for this specific MS-ISAC pilot.

projects.Use Case: Agentic AI for arrears and collections management
projects.Project Summary: Target Group deployed Collections Guru, an agentic AI collections assistant co-developed by Tech Mahindra and AWS, to gather and interpret case data, guide advisers and optimize collection strategies in arrears-management workflows.
projects.Scale: Deployed in parts of Target Group's arrears-management operation; exact adviser, case and rollout counts were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Consolidate fragmented case information and automate collection-strategy preparation to reduce handling time, screen switching and reliance on specialist subject knowledge.
projects.Measured Metric: Company-reported efficiency gain in deployed areas
projects.Notes: Tech Mahindra says the deployed solution delivered about 40% efficiency gains, while Target's COO described these as encouraging early results and anticipated gains in rolled-out areas. Treat the figure as preliminary, self-reported evidence; exact rollout size, measurement period and methodology were not disclosed.

projects.Use Case: Humanoid robot production and commercial rollout
projects.Project Summary: XPENG commissioned dedicated automated production lines for its IRON general-purpose humanoid robot and completed the first line-manufactured unit, moving the program from R&D prototyping into production-line manufacturing ahead of planned commercial rollout.
projects.Scale: First line-produced IRON completed; core-process automation exceeds 80%; mass production targeted by end-2026; China and overseas market deliveries planned for 2027
projects.Economic Mechanism: Move humanoid robots from prototype builds to repeatable automotive-grade manufacturing and commercial deployment
projects.Notes: Production-line commissioning and the first line-produced unit are operating milestones, but mass production and external delivery remain prospective. The >80% automation figure is company-reported and does not establish throughput, yield, cost, or customer demand.

projects.Use Case: Autonomous surface-vessel operations with Navy fleets
projects.Project Summary: Leidos' LAVA maritime-autonomy system moved further into fleet operations: Sea Hunter completed autonomous RIMPAC operations and Seahawk became the first medium uncrewed surface vessel to deploy operationally with a U.S. carrier strike group.
projects.Scale: Sea Hunter autonomously traveled more than 2,000 nautical miles from Pearl Harbor to San Diego after RIMPAC; Seahawk is operating with the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group
projects.Economic Mechanism: Extend naval capacity with uncrewed vessels operating within fleet communications, command-and-control, and operational frameworks
projects.Notes: Sea Hunter and Seahawk are separate vessels linked by the same LAVA autonomy architecture and Navy operational-integration effort. Leidos' portfolio-wide autonomy mileage and safe-hours figures are not treated as project-specific results.

projects.Use Case: Personal AI agent for cross-application task execution
projects.Project Summary: Meta launched Muse in the United States as a persistent personal AI agent that can use the web and connected services to complete multi-step tasks including email, travel booking, forms, negotiation and purchases, with user approval required for sensitive actions.
projects.Scale: U.S. rollout across iOS, Android and muse.ai, with access through the Muse app and WhatsApp; active-user count not disclosed
projects.Economic Mechanism: Automate consumer knowledge-work and transaction workflows through a persistent agent operating in a dedicated secure virtual machine
projects.Notes: Launch availability is not evidence of adoption. Reuters reported that Meta delayed Muse for additional security work and that internal testing surfaced disconnections, unprompted uploads and serious privacy/security failures; Meta said the launch version meets its safety and privacy bar while acknowledging errors can still occur.

projects.Use Case: Dedicated AI compute capacity for OpenAI in Malaysia
projects.Project Summary: Firmus and OpenAI entered a multi-year partnership under which OpenAI will contract dedicated compute from two Firmus AI Factory sites in Malaysia, making OpenAI an anchor customer for Firmus' regional AI-infrastructure buildout.
projects.Scale: Two Malaysia AI Factory sites for OpenAI; Firmus reports more than 900 MW of contracted capacity across all customers and five portfolio sites under development
projects.Economic Mechanism: Provide dedicated regional training and inference capacity through integrated AI factories built around next-generation NVIDIA systems
projects.Notes: The more-than-900-MW figure is Firmus' portfolio-wide contracted capacity, not OpenAI's Malaysia allocation. The two Malaysia sites are not yet operating; site-specific capacity, contract value and ready-for-service dates were not disclosed.

projects.Use Case: Driverless long-haul commercial trucking
projects.Project Summary: Kodiak AI is completing the safety case for a planned driverless long-haul commercial launch, reporting that its company-defined Autonomy Readiness Measure reached 93% at the end of August as final engineering verification, validation and testing continue.
projects.Scale: Autonomy Readiness Measure at 93% at end-August, up from 91% at end-July; commercial driverless long-haul launch targeted by year-end 2026
projects.Economic Mechanism: Remove the onboard driver from long-haul freight while using a structured safety case to validate readiness for commercial deployment
projects.Notes: ARM is Kodiak's own measure of the share of safety-case claims and evidence it considers materially complete, not an independent safety score or probability of safe operation. Kodiak's 35 driverless Permian Basin trucks are a separate industrial use case and are not counted as long-haul commercial deployment.

projects.Use Case: Lithography manufacturing-capacity expansion
projects.Project Summary: ASML broke ground on its new BIC North industrial campus in Eindhoven, a second major production campus that will add production, logistics, cleanroom and office capacity and a Flow Factory intended to accelerate scalable module production and installation.
projects.Scale: Approximately 350,000 square meters; potential capacity up to 20,000 workplaces; first phase targeted for 2029 with at least 3,000 employees
projects.Economic Mechanism: Increase lithography manufacturing throughput and capacity as AI-driven demand expands advanced processor and memory production
projects.Notes: Construction has started, but no new BIC North manufacturing capacity is operating yet. Reuters reported nearly all EUV capacity is booked through the end of 2027; the 20,000-workplace figure is the site's potential ultimate capacity, not current employment or lithography-tool output.

projects.Use Case: Commercial robotaxi ride-hailing
projects.Project Summary: Pony.ai and Mowasalat operate a fare-charging Robotaxi service in Doha through the Karwa app; the commercial pilot has operated since December 2025 with trained safety operators onboard, while Gen-7 Robotaxis were demonstrated without an onboard safety operator at the September 2026 AEMOB Forum.
projects.Scale: Fare-charging commercial pilot through the Karwa app; trained safety operators remain onboard in normal service; fully driverless Gen-7 demonstrated at AEMOB Forum; fleet size not disclosed
projects.Economic Mechanism: Add autonomous ride-hailing capacity through Qatar's national mobility network while using Mowasalat's local fleet operations and rider access
projects.Notes: The fare-charging service is a real commercial pilot, but normal rides still use trained safety operators. The driverless Gen-7 operation disclosed on Sept. 9 was an AEMOB Forum demonstration, not evidence that ordinary Doha commercial rides are yet driverless. Pony.ai's broader overseas deployment targets are not treated as Doha-specific scale.

projects.Use Case: Autonomous hospitality-service robotics
projects.Project Summary: MBody AI completed a proof-of-concept deployment of autonomous robots at Mohegan Sun in Connecticut; the robots remained in service after the pilot and converted to a paid commercial agreement across gaming-floor and conference-center operations.
projects.Scale: Robots operate full day and evening shifts across the gaming floor and conference center; fleet count not disclosed; a larger multi-year subscription expansion is under negotiation for later 2026
projects.Economic Mechanism: Automate repetitive, time-sensitive hospitality tasks and shift staff time toward higher-value guest-facing work
projects.Notes: The current paid commercial engagement is operating. The proposed larger multi-year expansion is still being negotiated and should not be treated as signed or deployed. Exact fleet size, task counts and project-specific ROI were not disclosed.

projects.Use Case: Autonomous clinical AI agent for heart-failure care
projects.Project Summary: Tempus received an ARPA-H ADVOCATE award to build and clinically validate a patient-facing autonomous AI agent for heart-failure care that continuously monitors clinical and home data and can manage symptoms, medications, virtual rehabilitation and scheduling while coordinating through the electronic health record.
projects.Scale: Up to $9.5 million ARPA-H award; multi-center prospective validation study planned; patient count, center count and deployment timeline not disclosed
projects.Economic Mechanism: Extend scarce cardiology capacity with continuous AI-supported heart-failure management and close gaps in guideline-recommended care
projects.Notes: This is a funded build and planned clinical-validation program, not yet a clinically validated autonomous-care deployment. Existing Tempus products cited as technical foundations should not be counted as outcomes of the ADVOCATE project.

projects.Use Case: Generative AI call summarization for customer-care centers
projects.Project Summary: Truist fully deployed AI Call Summaries across its care centers, automatically turning client conversations into structured summaries for follow-up and post-call documentation.
projects.Scale: More than 4.5 million summaries generated in Q2 2026; supported more than 70% of care-center inbound interactions; fully deployed across Truist care centers
projects.Economic Mechanism: Automate note-taking and post-call documentation to reduce teammate administrative time and improve continuity across client interactions
projects.Notes: Truist reports average time savings of about 30 seconds per call and more than 36,000 teammate hours saved in Q2 2026. The result is company-reported and derived from the stated average time-saving assumption; no independent evaluation was disclosed.

projects.Use Case: In-orbit AI processing for earth observation and sovereign intelligence
projects.Project Summary: Marlan Space and Loft Orbital are leading the Altair-Next Gen consortium to build an initial 50-satellite constellation combining radar, optical and other sensors with onboard AI and continuous connectivity so observations can be processed in orbit and delivered as alerts within seconds.
projects.Scale: Initial 50-satellite constellation; first 10 satellites already in production at Orbitworks in Abu Dhabi; $1 billion investment in France; first AI-enabled satellite targeted for launch in October 2026
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce observation-to-alert latency from hours to seconds by processing sensor data in orbit and share satellite infrastructure across sovereign and commercial programs
projects.Notes: The 50-satellite figure is a planned initial constellation, not deployed capacity. The first 10 are in production. WAM says the first of the Abu Dhabi-built satellites is expected to launch in the next few weeks; Aletihad reports the first AI-enabled satellite is scheduled for October 2026. Marketing descriptions such as 'world's largest' are not treated as analytical rankings.

projects.Use Case: Fully driverless robotaxi commercialization in Zagreb
projects.Project Summary: Pony.ai and Verne began fully driverless Robotaxi test rides with passengers on public roads in Zagreb, advancing an existing commercial service from onboard-operator operation toward unsupervised commercial service.
projects.Scale: Fully driverless passenger tests on a 22-km route linking Verne headquarters/business district with Zagreb Airport; the underlying commercial service has logged more than 200,000 km and several thousand customer rides with an onboard AV operator.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Remove the onboard operator from an already operating ride-hailing service while preserving local fleet operations and Uber distribution.
projects.Notes: The new fully driverless operation is approved passenger testing, not yet evidence of unsupervised commercial service. The 200,000-km and several-thousand-ride figures refer to the existing Zagreb commercial service while an onboard AV operator was still used.

projects.Use Case: AI-assisted semiconductor and AI-system supply-chain operations
projects.Project Summary: NVIDIA began deploying a Palantir/Nemotron sovereign AI stack inside its own supply chain to identify constraints, support materials-allocation decisions, codify operational expertise and coordinate the path from components to finished AI systems.
projects.Scale: Initial internal deployment focused on NVIDIA supply-chain teams and materials-allocation decisions; NVIDIA says its supply chain spans millions of parts, thousands of suppliers and a global manufacturing network.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Use governed proprietary operational data to surface supply constraints earlier and speed materials-allocation decisions across a highly interdependent AI-hardware supply chain.
projects.Notes: The deployment is operating internally, but NVIDIA disclosed no measured cycle-time, inventory, cost, yield or throughput improvement. Supplier/part-count descriptions establish operational complexity rather than a quantified AI benefit.

projects.Use Case: Agentic procurement and purchase-order automation
projects.Project Summary: StarLink put IBM Bob- and watsonx Orchestrate-based AI agents into its own procurement operations to automate email intake, document processing, ERP validation, quote comparison and accounts-payable execution across an end-to-end purchase-order workflow.
projects.Scale: Client Zero deployment across procurement workflows; annual workload cited includes 9,000 purchase orders and 14,000 quotes.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce manual procurement processing and coordination across email, unstructured documents, ERP and accounts-payable systems.
projects.Notes: StarLink reports quote comparison fell from 30 minutes to 3 minutes and AI-agent implementation from about two weeks to two days. The separately stated 11,500 annual hours saved is a projection, not a realized audited annual result.

projects.Use Case: Dedicated Blackwell B300 capacity for a GPU cloud marketplace
projects.Project Summary: QumulusAI completed deployment and full customer handoff of NVIDIA Blackwell B300 capacity at its Philadelphia colocation site for an unnamed GPU cloud marketplace, activating a two-year take-or-pay agreement.
projects.Scale: Full contracted B300 capacity live at a Philadelphia colocation site; $18 million two-year take-or-pay agreement; customer serves AI teams in more than 100 regions; GPU count not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Convert contracted inference demand into live dedicated GPU capacity using distributed colocation infrastructure and available pockets of power.
projects.Notes: Full customer handoff was reached Sept. 1, 2026, so this is deployed production capacity rather than an announced contract. The customer and GPU count were not disclosed; the $18 million is contracted value, not recognized revenue or utilization.

projects.Use Case: Agentic knowledge retrieval for proposal creation and customer support
projects.Project Summary: PLDT deployed KAI, an agentic knowledge assistant grounded in approved enterprise sources, to replace manual research for proposal creation and customer support with contextual responses delivered in seconds.
projects.Scale: Knowledge retrieval reduced from an up-to-five-day manual process to 1-3 seconds; PLDT estimates 25,000-30,000 hours of manual effort saved annually and roughly 12 FTE-equivalent productivity capacity.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce research time and expand service/sales capacity without proportional headcount growth.
projects.Notes: Benefits are PLDT/UiPath estimates; user count, measurement period and calculation methodology were not disclosed. The 12 FTE-equivalent figure is productivity capacity, not reported headcount elimination.

projects.Use Case: AI-powered enterprise sales and customer-service assistant
projects.Project Summary: PLDT deployed Ellie, an internal AI-powered digital assistant that connects enterprise knowledge and workflows to support customer engagement, proposal creation and solution enablement.
projects.Scale: PLDT reports 25-35% less manual effort, an estimated 18,000-25,000 hours saved annually, and customer response times up to 80% faster; deployment size and request volume were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Connect fragmented knowledge, people and systems to shorten preparation and customer-response cycles.
projects.Notes: Reported improvements are company estimates and not independently audited. The disclosure does not establish whether Ellie's annual hours-saved estimate overlaps with benefits attributed to KAI.

projects.Use Case: Agentic enterprise risk assessment and review
projects.Project Summary: PLDT and Smart deployed ERICA, an agentic risk-management system that synthesizes organizational inputs, scores risks and recommends treatments while retaining human review and validation.
projects.Scale: Deployed in February 2026; PLDT reports complex risk evaluations fell from 2-10 days to 5 minutes-1 day and manual effort fell 97-99%. Business-unit and review-volume counts were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce analyst workload and cycle time as enterprise risk reviews become more frequent and detailed.
projects.Notes: PLDT says human oversight remains central and outputs are reviewed by risk professionals. The 97-99% reduction is company-reported and not independently audited.

projects.Use Case: Governed enterprise AI gateway for LLM, agent and MCP traffic
projects.Project Summary: Sportsbet deployed TrueFoundry as a self-hosted AI gateway inside its AWS environment to centralize governance, observability, access control and routing for LLM traffic and MCP-connected agent tool calls across engineering workflows.
projects.Scale: Initially scoped to developer-built and developer-used agents; an existing production PRD/user-story agent was re-platformed through the gateway, with additional defect-detection and coding-assistant workflows being built. Call volume and team count were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Create a common governed control plane so production AI agents can scale across tools and model providers without losing auditability or access control.
projects.Notes: The provider disclosure includes direct Sportsbet customer quotes but no measured adoption, cost or business-outcome results. Product-level latency/RPS marketing claims are not treated as project outcomes.

projects.Use Case: AI-generated robotic arc-welding programming
projects.Project Summary: FANUC and Google developed an AI Welding Agent that reads engineering drawings, generates welding parameters and robot-motion programs, and can execute arc welding on FANUC CRX robots with zero setup and zero teaching.
projects.Scale: Live demonstration scheduled from September 16, 2026; shipments are scheduled to begin by the end of December 2026. The system uses the CRX teach-pendant camera and does not require additional site cameras.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce robot-programming and welding-setup labor and shorten production lead times amid a shortage of skilled welders.
projects.Notes: The source is an unedited mirror of a FANUC corporate release. This is a developed prototype/product launch, not evidence of customer field deployment. Operators may fine-tune AI-generated parameters before welding.

projects.Use Case: Frontier-scale sovereign AI compute cluster
projects.Project Summary: G42 and Khazna are constructing the 1 GW Stargate UAE cluster within the broader 5 GW UAE-US AI Campus. September 11 reporting says regional security threats are prompting review of the broader campus design, including more distributed and hardened infrastructure, while G42 says work is progressing as planned.
projects.Scale: 1 GW Stargate UAE cluster under construction; first 200 MW is expected to go live in 2026. The broader UAE-US AI Campus is planned for 5 GW but is not current operating capacity.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Expand regional frontier compute capacity while hardening critical AI infrastructure against physical-security and continuity risks.
projects.Enabling Vendors: Khazna Data Centers; OpenAI; Oracle; NVIDIA; Cisco; SoftBank
projects.Notes: Reuters' September 11 redesign details rely on sources familiar with the review and are not a finalized blueprint. G42 says project specifics remain under continuous review. Do not treat the 5 GW campus figure or the 1 GW Stargate figure as live capacity.

projects.Use Case: Large-scale AI data-center campus in Cameron County, Texas
projects.Project Summary: Fluidstack began site work on the first phase of a large AI data-center campus in Cameron County, Texas, after the county issued a worksite permit covering clearing, grading, utilities, roads and stormwater infrastructure.
projects.Scale: More than 1,100 acres; approximately $4B planned first-phase investment; site work underway; phase one targeted for completion by mid-2028; IT load not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Create new AI-compute capacity through a purpose-built campus with self-funded site and power infrastructure.
projects.Notes: The current county permit advances site preparation but does not authorize all future building work; additional permits remain required. The disclosed $4B is planned first-phase investment, not realized spend, and the project has not disclosed operating IT load or online compute capacity.

projects.Use Case: Autonomous intra-hub pallet and inventory transport
projects.Project Summary: CEVA Logistics launched a pilot at its Blue Hub using Zelostech Z10 autonomous electric vehicles to move pallets, totes and inventory between areas and floors using the facility's existing multi-level ramps.
projects.Scale: Two Z10 autonomous electric vehicles deployed at the approximately 50,000-square-meter, eight-story Blue Hub; throughput, utilization and cost results were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Automate repetitive intra-hub transport, increase scheduling flexibility and replace diesel-powered movements with electric autonomous vehicles.
projects.Notes: This is a live pilot, not evidence of full-site autonomous conversion. The disclosures do not provide delivery throughput, labor savings, safety outcomes or unit economics.

projects.Use Case: Agentic customer support during NFL Sunday Ticket demand
projects.Project Summary: YouTube deployed a Gemini Enterprise customer-support agent with Google Cloud and Accenture during NFL Sunday Ticket surge demand, using the agent to help handle high-volume customer interactions.
projects.Scale: Deployed during NFL Sunday Ticket surge demand; Accenture reports 37% lower average handle time and an 11% improvement in customer sentiment; interaction volume and measurement methodology were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce support handling time and improve customer experience during concentrated demand spikes.
projects.Notes: The 37% handle-time reduction and 11% sentiment improvement are partner-reported results. The disclosure does not provide the conversation count, baseline period or measurement methodology.

projects.Use Case: NVIDIA DSX AI-factory capacity at the Bundey campus
projects.Project Summary: IREN is applying NVIDIA's DSX AI-factory architecture across its development portfolio, including its planned Bundey campus in South Australia, to build integrated accelerated-computing infrastructure for AI workloads.
projects.Scale: Bundey is planned as an 800 MW campus; the capacity is not yet operating. NVIDIA's separate up-to-2-GW-by-2027 figure applies across eight Australian infrastructure partners, not to IREN alone.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Turn large-scale power and data-center development into standardized accelerated-computing capacity for AI customers.
projects.Notes: The 800 MW figure is planned campus scale, not live GPU or IT capacity. Do not attribute NVIDIA's ecosystem-wide 2 GW target to IREN or treat it as current operating capacity.

projects.Use Case: AI data flywheel for autonomous-driving development and validation
projects.Project Summary: Hyundai Motor Group put its autonomous-driving Data Flywheel into full operation, linking real-world driving-data collection with AI training, validation and redeployment through 42dot's Atria AI development workflow.
projects.Scale: Approximately 40 dedicated data-collection vehicles operate around the clock; the framework is being standardized across Hyundai Motor, Kia, 42dot and Motional, with broader fleet data integration planned.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Shorten autonomous-driving model development and validation cycles by continuously feeding difficult real-world driving cases back into training and deployment.
projects.Notes: The Data Flywheel is operating as an internal engineering system, but Hyundai has not disclosed a measured development-time or safety-performance improvement. The approximately 40 vehicles are dedicated data-collection vehicles; annual group vehicle sales are not equivalent to connected training-data volume, and current Atria AI demonstrations are not commercial Level 4 service.

projects.Use Case: Level 4 autonomous heavy-duty trucking
projects.Project Summary: Pony.ai and GAC Commercial Vehicle unveiled a tested and validated Gen-4 Level 4 heavy-duty Robotruck on GAC's T9 battery-electric platform, moving the program toward planned volume production and deployment in long-haul, dedicated-route and port logistics.
projects.Scale: Gen-4 T9 Robotruck formally unveiled after vehicle testing and validation; volume production scheduled later in 2026; planned use cases include long-haul freight, dedicated-route logistics and port transportation.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce autonomous-trucking hardware and operating costs while moving a validated L4 truck design into repeatable vehicle production and freight deployment.
projects.Notes: The 70% ADK bill-of-materials reduction is company-reported versus the prior generation. Volume production, a 30% reduction in transportation cost per ton-kilometer and a 10% reduction in energy consumption remain forward-looking and are not treated as realized deployment economics.

projects.Use Case: In-house electrical-equipment manufacturing for AI data centers
projects.Project Summary: Crusoe opened a second Tulsa manufacturing facility to build medium-voltage switchgear, low-voltage switchboards, electrical enclosures, industrial controls and copper busbar used in large-scale AI data-center construction.
projects.Scale: Second Tulsa factory adds 400,000 square feet; roughly 1 million square feet of national manufacturing footprint; more than 300 Tulsa craft workers; more than 2,500 switchboards supplied to Crusoe's Stargate site in Abilene.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Vertically integrate critical electrical-equipment production to compress component lead times and expand the pace at which powered AI data-center infrastructure can be built.
projects.Measured Metric: Switchboards supplied to Abilene Stargate site
projects.Notes: Crusoe says in-house production can turn around some components in days versus industry timelines that often take months; treat that as a company characterization rather than an independently measured lead-time benchmark. The more-than-2,500 switchboards are supplied to the Abilene Stargate site, not a daily or annual production-rate metric.

projects.Use Case: Liquid-cooled AI cloud capacity for rack-scale GPU systems
projects.Project Summary: Bitdeer AI secured A202, a 65.1 MW AI Cloud data-center facility on its existing Johor Bahru campus under a 10-year data-center-services agreement, targeting liquid-cooled rack-scale NVIDIA systems for GPU cloud and data-hosting workloads.
projects.Scale: 65.1 MW critical IT load at A202; Johor A201 plus A202 totals 86.8 MW; total secured AI Cloud data-center capacity approximately 206.5 MW; A202 energization targeted for Q3 2027.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reuse an existing campus's power, cooling and network infrastructure to shorten the path to powered AI-cloud capacity and contract customer demand ahead of energization.
projects.Notes: A202 is secured but not energized. The company expects energization in Q3 2027 and had not disclosed signed A202 customer offtake in the announcement. Bitdeer's more-than-$7B active AI Cloud pipeline is a management estimate of potential contract value under discussion, not backlog, revenue or executed contracts.

projects.Use Case: Production computer-vision inference and research infrastructure
projects.Project Summary: Roboflow runs its production computer-vision inference and research workloads on Crusoe Cloud and Crusoe Managed Kubernetes across two data centers after moving from a short GPU proof of concept to reserved production capacity.
projects.Scale: All 300,000+ Roboflow computer-vision models run on Crusoe infrastructure; more than 69,000 distinct models are served monthly; the serverless system handles hundreds of millions of requests per month across two data centers.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Secure dedicated GPU headroom and offload Kubernetes operations to support unpredictable low-latency vision demand while reducing infrastructure-management labor and hyperscaler cost overhead.
projects.Measured Metric: Infrastructure engineers freed from Kubernetes operations
projects.Notes: The 2-3 engineer figure is Roboflow's estimate of the staffing burden avoided by managed Kubernetes, not reported layoffs or an independently audited productivity result. The case study is provider-published but includes named Roboflow customer executives and operating metrics; 300,000+ refers to models, not customers.

projects.Use Case: Driverless retail freight on public roads
projects.Project Summary: Einride and Lidl Germany deployed a cab-less SAE Level 4 electric truck with no onboard driver or safety operator into daily public-road store-delivery operations in Edermünde under a German Federal Motor Transport Authority permit.
projects.Scale: One cab-less truck; up to 3 trips per day; 15 Euro-pallet positions; the four-month project can move more than 3,000 pallets and covers dry-goods delivery on the route.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Operate scheduled store deliveries without an onboard driver, easing driver-capacity constraints while maintaining daily freight continuity.
projects.Enabling Vendors: Einride; Schwarz Corporate Solutions; Schwarz Digits
projects.Notes: The KBA permit enables defined SAE Level 4 operation on public roads and is described as the first of its kind in Germany. The more-than-3,000-pallet figure is project-period transport capacity, not realized throughput. Route expansion and further deployments remain prospective.

projects.Use Case: Agentic customer-service workflow automation
projects.Project Summary: Air India expanded Salesforce Agentforce beyond refund processing into automated multi-intent email resolution, passenger name-change automation and a real-time knowledge agent, with AI agents validating requests and taking actions across enterprise systems under confidence thresholds and human oversight.
projects.Scale: Refund processing plus three expanded customer-service workflows are deployed; exact interaction, user and rollout counts were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Orchestrate validations, approvals and backend actions across customer-service systems to shorten resolution cycles and reduce repetitive agent work.
projects.Notes: Air India reports internal refund processing fell from approximately 14 days to about 4 hours; bank processing time is unchanged. Name-change turnaround fell from about three days to 30 minutes. Eligible automated email responses require more than 95% confidence, with human oversight where required. Results are customer/vendor reported and not independently audited.

projects.Use Case: AI agreement intelligence and document processing
projects.Project Summary: Docusign runs a production AI pipeline for Intelligent Agreement Management using task-specific models and context engineering on Microsoft Azure to extract agreement intelligence and power downstream automation at enterprise scale.
projects.Scale: IAM processes more than 1 million agreement documents per day; Agreement Manager is the first production application of the optimized model architecture.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce inference cost and latency per agreement while preserving extraction accuracy so high-volume agreement intelligence remains economically viable.
projects.Enabling Vendors: Microsoft Azure; Microsoft Foundry; Azure OpenAI
projects.Notes: Docusign reports up to eightfold document-processing throughput while maintaining extraction accuracy within two percentage points of larger models and cutting AI processing costs by 90%. The case study is provider-published but includes named Docusign technical executives; more than 1 million documents per day is IAM-wide volume, not necessarily one model task.

projects.Use Case: Unified clinical and genomic data for AI-powered diabetes care
projects.Project Summary: M42 plans to deploy Oracle Health Data Intelligence, integrated with Oracle Health Foundation EHR, to unify clinical, genomic and real-world data and support AI-driven precision care, beginning with its diabetes programs.
projects.Scale: Initial deployment is planned within M42 diabetes programs; exact sites, patient count and deployment timing were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Centralize fragmented healthcare data so clinicians and researchers can generate predictive insights, coordinate care and engage chronic-disease patients more proactively.
projects.Notes: This is a clearly scoped planned deployment, not an operating measured result. M42's wider network of more than 480 facilities is not treated as project scope. Existing Emirati Genome Program data integration into the EHR predates this Oracle Health Data Intelligence deployment.

projects.Use Case: AI-assisted customer self-service and virtual agents
projects.Project Summary: Voya Financial operates AI-enabled customer-support features across multiple Workplace business lines, including virtual agents and self-service systems that resolve millions of customer interactions annually.
projects.Scale: 7 million annual AI-enabled customer interactions; more than 2.8 million calls resolved through AI-assisted self-service; virtual agents report 85% digital resolution and 96% positive feedback.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Resolve routine customer needs through AI self-service so human service capacity can focus on interactions that require higher-touch support.
projects.Notes: The more-than-2.8-million call figure is reported within Voya's 7-million annual AI-enabled interaction volume. The 85% digital-resolution and 96% positive-feedback figures are company-reported; no independent evaluation or exact baseline was disclosed.

projects.Use Case: Enterprise AI coworker across banker and employee workflows
projects.Project Summary: Fulton Bank deployed Salesforce Agentforce Coworker across internal workflows, moving from zero to more than 20 production use cases in a matter of weeks with the assistant operating inside existing Salesforce permissions and business rules.
projects.Scale: More than 20 use cases live in production supporting approximately 3,000 users; Fulton reports substantial daily usage.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Let employees retrieve context, prepare work and take governed actions across Salesforce data and specialized agents without building separate interfaces or permissions systems.
projects.Notes: The scale and usage statements come from a named Fulton Bank executive in Salesforce's launch disclosure. No measured time savings, task volume, error-rate improvement or financial outcome was disclosed.

projects.Use Case: Predictive drone positioning and rooftop order loading
projects.Project Summary: Flytrex launched rooftop docking and predictive AI positioning at active Dallas-Fort Worth merchant locations so drones can be prepositioned before orders arrive and restaurant staff can load them directly without a dedicated runner.
projects.Scale: Launching at active DFW merchant locations; installation of more than 100 additional sites is underway; Flytrex's broader U.S. network has completed more than 250,000 deliveries.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Remove runner labor and the pickup flight, while increasing aircraft utilization, to lower cost and delivery time for autonomous food delivery.
projects.Notes: Flytrex also reports customer delivery time is reduced by half. The 60% cost reduction and time improvement are company-reported without a disclosed baseline, sample size or independent audit; more than 250,000 deliveries refers to Flytrex's broader U.S. history, not the new dock system.

projects.Use Case: High-density AI data-center capacity at Niagara Falls
projects.Project Summary: Blockfusion signed a definitive long-term anchor lease with CoreWeave for AI data-center capacity at its Niagara Falls campus and a companion expansion agreement, replacing the non-binding anchor-tenant LOI announced in June.
projects.Scale: 15-year initial anchor lease with two five-year renewal options; contracted critical IT load, lease value and delivery schedule were not disclosed in the definitive announcement.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Convert an already-interconnected, low-carbon power site into contracted high-density AI capacity for CoreWeave while avoiding a greenfield interconnection path.
projects.Notes: The definitive agreement confirms the tenant and lease term but does not disclose the contracted MW, price or delivery schedule. Do not carry the June LOI's proposed 85 MW guaranteed / up-to-300 MW economics forward as definitive contract terms. The campus's existing grid interconnection and low-carbon power are central to its AI conversion.

projects.Use Case: On-demand autonomous urban transit pilot
projects.Project Summary: May Mobility's autonomous-driving software is operating in a six-month Nagoya pilot led by NTT group companies and Aichi Prefecture, integrating autonomous vehicles with on-demand dispatch across a complex central-city route.
projects.Scale: Three autonomous vehicles; five boarding/alighting locations; weekday operations from September 11, 2026 through March 19, 2027.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Validate autonomous driving and on-demand fleet operations in dense urban traffic as a step toward Level 4 service and scalable local transit.
projects.Enabling Vendors: NTT Docomo Business; NTT Docomo; Meitetsu Taxi Holdings
projects.Notes: NTT says the pilot is intended to improve intersection control, opposing-vehicle handling on right turns and signal-timing prediction while testing the integration of autonomous-driving software with on-demand dispatch. The current pilot is a validation program toward Level 4, not evidence of driverless Level 4 commercial service.

projects.Use Case: AI coding agents for design-system component delivery
projects.Project Summary: Bolt deployed AI coding agents in its front-end design pipeline so designers can ship working UI components directly into the production library under a unified review model.
projects.Scale: bolt.eu serves up to 60 million users annually across 50+ markets; shared design system has more than 110 UI components; exact designer and agent usage counts were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Reduce design-to-engineering handoffs and component-delivery cycle time while keeping production review in one workflow.
projects.Notes: Bolt reports routine component delivery fell from about one week to about one hour after replacing informal handoffs with an AI-agent-enabled pipeline and unified review model. The result is company-reported and does not establish aggregate engineering productivity or headcount effects.

projects.Use Case: AI agents for frontier-model research and engineering
projects.Project Summary: Anthropic operates a large internal Claude-agent system across AI research and engineering, with agents completing increasingly large portions of model-development work under human supervision and continuous monitoring.
projects.Scale: Approximately 30,000 research and engineering agents active at any one time on Anthropic's most-used internal platform; more than 1 billion agent decisions analyzed in August 2026.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Accelerate frontier-model R&D by delegating substantial research and engineering work to supervised AI agents while preserving intervention and auditability.
projects.Measured Metric: AI R&D work led by Claude
projects.Notes: Anthropic's prototype Automation Index says Claude leads 26% of measured AI R&D and collaborates or leads on more than 90%, but no measured subset is fully autonomous. Metrics are self-reported and partly model-judged; Anthropic plans third-party verification.

projects.Use Case: Agentic grid-planning and interconnection studies
projects.Project Summary: AWS and Duke Energy deployed specialized AI agents into utility interconnection-study workflows to automate data preparation, coordinate physics-based simulations and help engineers analyze grid-upgrade options while retaining final human engineering decisions.
projects.Scale: Duke Energy engineers are using the agents in interconnection-study workflows; AWS says the program is available to qualified utilities and grid operators, but customer count and study volume were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Increase scarce power-systems-engineering capacity and shorten interconnection-study preparation so generation and large-load projects can move through grid planning faster.
projects.Notes: AWS reports Duke Energy reduced some data-preparation tasks from two weeks of manual work to hours. The disclosure does not quantify the exact hour count, full-study cycle-time reduction, completed-study volume or downstream interconnection acceleration.

projects.Use Case: Fully autonomous ride-hailing across European cities
projects.Project Summary: Lucid and Bolt announced a strategic partnership to develop and deploy Level 4 autonomous ride-hailing services in Europe using vehicles from Lucid's upcoming Midsize platform, NVIDIA Hyperion and Bolt's mobility network and operating infrastructure.
projects.Scale: Bolt aims to deploy at least 25,000 fully autonomous Lucid vehicles across multiple European cities and countries; initial launch cities, timing and current partnership fleet were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Build large-scale autonomous ride supply on Bolt's network using a purpose-built vehicle platform, autonomy compute and shared fleet operations.
projects.Notes: The 25,000-vehicle figure is a prospective deployment target, not a current fleet or firm delivered order. Bolt's separate ambition for 100,000 autonomous vehicles by 2035 spans its broader platform and should not be attributed to this Lucid partnership alone.

projects.Use Case: SiGe manufacturing capacity for AI data-center optical connectivity
projects.Project Summary: GlobalFoundries and Marvell expanded a multi-year manufacturing agreement to add silicon-germanium capacity at GF's Burlington, Vermont facility for next-generation pluggable, near-packaged and co-packaged optical connectivity used in AI data centers.
projects.Scale: Expansion builds on existing Burlington SiGe production and is expected to add significant capacity; wafer output, investment, timing and customer shipment volumes were not disclosed.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Expand domestic semiconductor output for high-speed optical interconnects as AI-cluster bandwidth requirements and Marvell demand grow.
projects.Notes: The agreement is a concrete manufacturing-capacity expansion but does not disclose a numeric capacity target or delivery date. Existing production should not be treated as evidence that the incremental capacity is already online.

projects.Use Case: AI-agent optimization of biomolecular modeling software
projects.Project Summary: Anthropic used Claude to optimize more than 30 open-source biomolecular prediction and design models for speed and memory efficiency and released the optimized code for scientific use.
projects.Scale: More than 30 open-source biomolecular models optimized in just under four weeks; a low-memory mode enables accurate modeling of systems above 10,000 tokens on a single NVIDIA GPU node.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Lower the compute cost and engineering effort required to run scientific modeling workflows and expand the size of biomolecular systems that can be analyzed on accessible hardware.
projects.Notes: Anthropic reports roughly 4x average speedup and says the optimized code can achieve comparable in-silico protein-design performance using two orders of magnitude fewer GPU hours in a simplified workflow. These are research/engineering results, not measured downstream drug-discovery ROI or external production adoption.

projects.Use Case: Autonomous fixed-wing air logistics and remote flight operations
projects.Project Summary: Joby completed a 3,199-mile autonomous transcontinental flight with a converted Cessna Caravan using its autonomy stack, covering taxi, takeoff, cruise, rerouting and landing under remote supervision with zero control inputs from the onboard safety pilot.
projects.Scale: 3,199-mile eastbound autonomous flight; remote supervision from up to 2,323 miles away; autonomy stack has logged more than 400 flights and 800 automated flight hours.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Extend autonomous cargo, medical and defense logistics while reducing onboard pilot requirements and enabling remote operations over regional routes.
projects.Notes: The flight was a real-world demonstration, not unrestricted autonomous commercial service. An onboard safety pilot remained present but made zero control inputs; operations were remotely supervised, and related tour flights are being used to evaluate airspace integration with the FAA.

projects.Use Case: Fully autonomous commercial ride-hailing in Singapore
projects.Project Summary: Waymo announced a phased Singapore launch with the Ministry of Transport and Land Transport Authority, beginning with local fleet setup and 2027 readiness work before a planned fully autonomous commercial ride-hailing launch in 2028.
projects.Scale: Initial all-electric Jaguar I-PACE fleet expected to arrive in coming months; manual mapping and local adaptation planned in 2027; public commercial launch targeted for 2028.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Expand driverless ride-hailing into Southeast Asia through a regulator-coordinated, phased local validation and launch process.
projects.Enabling Vendors: Singapore Ministry of Transport; Land Transport Authority
projects.Notes: The 2028 service date is a forward-looking launch target, not current operating service. Waymo's 20 million rides and 300 million autonomous kilometres are platform-wide figures and are not treated as Singapore-specific scale.

projects.Use Case: Company-wide generative AI and AI-assisted software development
projects.Project Summary: Oracle rolled out ChatGPT Enterprise and OpenAI Codex across its workforce in April and May 2026, reaching broad adoption and sharply accelerating code generation while exposing downstream testing, validation, deployment and release-management constraints.
projects.Scale: Oracle's CIO organization supports about 160,000 employees; 80% adoption was reached within three months of the rollout.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Accelerate software creation and knowledge work, then redesign downstream engineering controls and model-routing economics so faster code generation translates into customer delivery.
projects.Notes: Business Insider reports internal town-hall statements from Oracle executives. Oracle says developers can generate in about a week code that previously took a team two to three quarters, but customer delivery has not accelerated because testing, validation, deployment and release management remain bottlenecks. The 80% adoption and productivity figures are company-reported and not independently audited.

projects.Use Case: AI-agent qualification and routing of inbound sales leads
projects.Project Summary: Siemens deployed two Agentforce agents to engage, qualify and route inbound sales leads using CRM data before handing the strongest opportunities to sellers.
projects.Scale: More than 2,500 unqualified inbound leads per month; 18,000 sellers; deployed across 132 countries; Siemens says 100% of these inbound leads are now engaged.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Automate top-of-funnel engagement and qualification so seller time is focused on higher-probability opportunities instead of manually screening every inbound lead.
projects.Notes: The disclosure is vendor-published but includes Siemens deployment details. The 100% figure is lead-engagement coverage, not a measured conversion-rate or revenue uplift; downstream partner-onboarding automation described in the same release remains forward-looking and is not counted as operating here.

projects.Use Case: National-scale autonomous trucking network
projects.Project Summary: HUMAIN and Applied Intuition announced a long-term commercial collaboration to build an autonomous logistics network in Saudi Arabia, beginning with driverless trucking on key freight corridors and using Applied Intuition's Self-Driving System and Vehicle OS.
projects.Scale: Thousands of autonomous trucks targeted across key Saudi logistics corridors by 2030; local Applied Intuition team and Riyadh office established.
projects.Economic Mechanism: Increase freight capacity and fleet utilization by operating trucks for longer periods while reducing dependence on scarce commercial-driving labor.
projects.Notes: The thousands-of-trucks figure is a 2030 target, not deployed Saudi fleet scale. Applied Intuition says its Self-Driving System is already operating on Level 4 trucks elsewhere, but that should not be treated as evidence that Saudi commercial autonomous trucking is operating today.

updates.Scale Before: Small initial commercial deployment in limited areas of Austin; expansion is planned gradually
updates.Scale After: Small initial commercial deployment in limited areas of Austin; expansion is planned gradually
updates.Summary: NHTSA required Tesla to answer detailed Cybercab self-certification questions by September 30, including whether temporary manual controls were used in the certification basis and what speed, geography, time-of-day and occupant-control restrictions apply.
updates.Notes: The audit remains open. NHTSA's information request is not a finding of noncompliance or a recall; existing federal safety standards remain in force while proposed AV rule changes are unfinished.

bottlenecks.Notes: Legacy v1 constraint normalized into v2 bottleneck taxonomy.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Electricity availability, transmission and construction remain gating constraints on realizing the planned capacity.
bottlenecks.Notes: Legacy v1 constraint normalized into v2 bottleneck taxonomy.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: SK hynix said the AI-driven memory shortage is expected to persist through 2030; the Indiana HBM packaging build is intended to expand and localize supply against that constraint.
bottlenecks.Notes: Constraint is sector-level memory supply but directly shapes the project's rationale and timing.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Meta's maintenance robots remain human-supervised and slower than technicians; reported limitations include battery downtime, navigation around cables/corners, grayscale vision that cannot distinguish red/green status lights, and inability to handle dense Nvidia GB300 cabling.
bottlenecks.Notes: Concrete operating constraints observed in live data-center trials; treat as reported pilot limitations, not a company-wide capability statement.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: MHS is explicitly aimed at replacing bespoke device integrations that can take weeks or months; the preview uses a shared interface so agents can discover and control programmable instruments across vendors.
bottlenecks.Notes: Integration is a concrete gating constraint for multi-instrument AI workflows; safety and reliability remain separate open issues during the preview.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Nscale designed Monarch around an onsite state-certified AI microgrid scalable to more than 8 GW, explicitly addressing powered-site availability as a gating constraint; the Anthropic agreement reportedly anchors about 460 MW of future compute capacity.
bottlenecks.Notes: The project addresses the power bottleneck through onsite generation rather than a conventional grid connection; construction, permitting and future chip delivery remain execution dependencies.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Changi's rollout is shaped by rising demand for reduced-mobility passenger assistance; the autonomous service removes the need for continuous one-to-one escort on eligible journeys, freeing ground staff for passengers who require higher-touch support.
bottlenecks.Notes: Treat this as a staffing-capacity constraint, not evidence of realized headcount reduction.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: The Oxagon build is explicitly shaped by access to large-scale energy resources, land and connectivity; NEOM and DataVolt say power availability, development speed, connectivity and operating efficiency are increasingly critical to AI-compute economics.
bottlenecks.Notes: The site is intended to address the power and infrastructure constraint; the first 100 MW remains under construction.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Google's need for scalable, round-the-clock electricity is directly shaping the project: the 396 MW PPA is intended to supply firm power for a potential Utah data center from Cape Station.
bottlenecks.Notes: The project is intended to address power availability; the related Google data-center build remains conditional and should not be treated as committed.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Waymo spent months validating the Driver on local streets before opening Denver, San Diego and Tampa, and is expanding rider access gradually rather than opening each market to everyone immediately.
bottlenecks.Notes: Treat reliability as an operating rollout constraint evidenced by local validation and staged access, not as evidence that the service is unsafe.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: The FAA is using eIPP demonstrations to identify regulatory and procedural gaps and support safe integration of advanced-air-mobility aircraft into the National Airspace System; Elroy's Houma flights remain part of that test framework rather than unrestricted commercial operations.
bottlenecks.Notes: Regulatory integration is directly gating broader autonomous cargo deployment; additional eIPP test flights are planned during 2026.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: BJC Health and WashU Medicine expanded Abridge from an initial 450-clinician rollout to roughly 4,000 clinicians after evaluation results and peer-to-peer clinician advocacy; strong user demand directly shaped the move to broader deployment.
bottlenecks.Notes: Adoption is recorded as an easing deployment gate rather than evidence of a current demand shortfall; the disclosed expansion was driven by clinician advocacy and measured pilot results.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: EcoHash used Cango's existing Georgia-site infrastructure and energy access to minimize new construction and accelerate the path from module delivery to GPU power-on, showing powered-site availability directly shaped deployment speed.
bottlenecks.Notes: Power is recorded as an easing gate because the project exploited an already-powered site; this does not imply power is unconstrained for future replication elsewhere.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: The London service launched only in supervised form with a trained TfL-licensed private-hire driver onboard, and Uber says fleet growth will proceed in line with readiness and regulation, so regulatory approval remains a concrete gate to unsupervised scale.
bottlenecks.Notes: This is not a safety-failure signal; it records the regulatory condition that the current public service remains supervised rather than driverless.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Cisco says action-taking enterprise agents need a governed architecture connecting approved models, approved systems and enterprise data pathways with human oversight; those controls directly shape MyAgent's cross-application execution design.
bottlenecks.Notes: Integration is the closest stable taxonomy label for the governed cross-system architecture Cisco describes as necessary to scale the agent. This is not evidence of a disclosed outage or failed rollout.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: QumulusAI activated all 616 contracted Blackwell GPUs across 77 nodes ahead of the Sept. 1 delivery target specifically to provide Runpod customers with additional production inference and agentic-workload capacity.
bottlenecks.Notes: Compute is recorded as an easing gate because reserved accelerator capacity was delivered and activated. The disclosure does not establish utilization levels or imply that Runpod's broader compute demand is fully met.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: HyperVault says the Hyderabad campus is being designed for higher-density AI with larger power blocks, green power and reliability, so power delivery directly shapes the site's architecture and phased capacity.
bottlenecks.Notes: Records power as a project-shaping infrastructure requirement, not evidence of a current outage or disclosed grid shortfall.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: NHTSA opened Audit Query AQ26002 to examine Tesla's self-certification of Cybercab without conventional manual controls while Tesla plans to expand commercial deployment gradually, making federal compliance a concrete gate to broader scale.
bottlenecks.Notes: The audit is an open compliance review, not a determination of noncompliance or a recall order.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government were deployed on GenAI.mil after accreditation at Impact Level 5 for Controlled Unclassified Information, showing security and compliance authorization as a concrete gate to department-wide frontier-model use.
bottlenecks.Notes: Records an easing compliance gate for CUI-capable enterprise use; it does not imply authorization for classified information above IL5.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: OpenAI says frontline essential-service defenders often operate with limited staff, budgets and specialized expertise; the MS-ISAC pilot therefore bundles Daybreak access with guided training and hands-on assistance rather than software access alone.
bottlenecks.Notes: Talent captures the program's stated staffing and expertise constraint. Budget limits are also discussed, but Capital is not separately recorded because the pilot bundles subsidized access and support.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Collections Guru gathers and interprets case data across systems and presents it in one adviser workflow; Target reported 40% less screen toggling and 30% lower handling time after deployment, showing fragmented system navigation was a concrete operating constraint the agent is reducing.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: XPENG commissioned dedicated humanoid-robot production lines with more than 80% of core processes automated, explicitly moving IRON from R&D prototyping toward repeatable line manufacturing, scaled production and rapid capacity expansion.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Seahawk became the first medium uncrewed surface vessel to deploy operationally with a U.S. carrier strike group inside its communications, command-and-control and operational framework, while Sea Hunter demonstrated manned-unmanned teaming at RIMPAC.
bottlenecks.Notes: Records an easing fleet-integration gate; it does not imply that all mission, reliability or communications constraints are solved.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Meta delayed Muse for additional security work, and Reuters reported internal testing surfaced disconnections, unprompted data uploads and serious privacy/security failures before launch; Meta says the released version meets its safety and privacy bar.
bottlenecks.Notes: The reporting establishes reliability and security as a concrete launch constraint, but it does not establish the failure rate or severity among production users.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Kodiak says the remaining work before removing the driver from long-haul commercial operations is concentrated in final engineering verification, validation and testing, with its company-defined Autonomy Readiness Measure at 93%.
bottlenecks.Notes: ARM is a company-defined completion measure for safety-case evidence, not an independent estimate of crash risk or launch probability.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: ASML started construction of BIC North while nearly all of its EUV capacity is booked through the end of 2027; the new campus includes a Flow Factory intended to make module production and installation faster and more scalable.

bottlenecks.Evidence Summary: Doha's fare-charging Robotaxi service operates under Qatar Ministry of Transport supervision with trained safety operators onboard, while fully driverless Gen-7 operation was demonstrated only at the AEMOB Forum, making authorization and operating integration a concrete gate to unsupervised commercial service.
